applied_items.content:
Gate lists. `chough gate list [--json]` SHALL number every open human gate of every open session in the project from 1, with the stage it holds and the native step it drives (REQ-cli-030). It SHALL give each a one-screen summary of at most 24 lines and 4,096 bytes, with:
- what changed: the change's ID and title joined with ` - `, never an em dash, then the files, insertions and deletions since the change's base, counted in the working tree so that uncommitted and untracked files count, as a change's own files are before they are committed, leaving out `.chough/`, the knowledge directory and SpecSync lifecycle bookkeeping, and naming the five files with the most changed lines among the rest (#190). At a gate that drives approval, the change's own definition, the Markdown files under `.specsync/changes/<id>/` (its `change.md`, deltas, plan and other artifacts), is what the human approves, so the summary SHALL count those files and name them first, its deltas before the change's other files with the requirement IDs each delta adds and those it modifies, each said as such, never leaving them out as bookkeeping. At a gate held at intent, the summary SHALL give the intent being approved in place of what changed when the session records no native change: each criterion the session references, by ID with its sentence from the HI file that holds it, and no diff line, since there is no base. The base is the change's own `base_commit` (from its `state.json`), so an earlier change on the same branch is not counted again. The base is instead the merge base of HEAD with the default branch (`origin/HEAD`, else `main`) in two cases: when that merge base is not an ancestor of the `base_commit`, meaning default-branch work was merged or rebased in after the change began (#190), and when the change records no `base_commit`. A merge base that is HEAD itself, as on the default branch, is not used. With no usable base, the summary says the base is unknown;
- the tests: how many cases passed, failed and were not run, by the latest observation of each case that links a requirement the change's deltas add or modify, or that the session's observations name, with the failing case IDs, and each observation the session names that links no case, counted by its own entry, so evidence recorded by `chough evidence add` with criteria and no case counts (#389);
- the risks: the first 8 lines of the change's `plan.md` section "Risks", or "none recorded";
- a diff link: the GitHub compare URL from the base to HEAD when `origin` is a GitHub remote, otherwise `git diff <base>..<HEAD>`; while the working tree holds changes since HEAD, the link SHALL be `git diff <base>`, which shows them, and SHALL say that work is not committed yet, never an empty `<base>..<base>` range (#389).

When the session records no base commit, as one started before the repository's first commit, and the repository has exactly one first commit, what changed and the diff SHALL count from that first commit and say so, naming why there is no base; with no commit at all they stay unknown (#389).

Each summary's digest SHALL be the SHA-256 of its text. The list SHALL be saved as `.chough/local/gate-lists/<list>.json`, where `<list>` is the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the list. Listing SHALL make no native read and write no tracked file. The list SHALL end with how to reply: `chough gate record` for the gates whose change is not verifying, and `chough change ship <id> --list <list> --gate <n>` for each gate whose change is verifying.

`chough gate record <list> --gates <n>[,<n>...] --decided-by <who> --words <words> --where <where> --recorded-by <agent>` SHALL close each named gate as `chough checkpoint --close-gate` would with the four values (REQ-cli-050), and its relay SHALL carry that gate's `summary_digest` and the `list` (REQ-history-014). It SHALL close all the named gates or none. Before writing anything, it SHALL refuse:
- an unknown list, a number not on it, a listed gate that is no longer open, or a gate whose summary's digest has changed, each naming `chough gate list`;
- a gate whose change's `state.json` state is `verifying`, naming `chough change ship <id> --list <list> --gate <n>` with the relay, and giving as the reason that such a gate closes through the ship, which runs the review as the human and closes the gate after the native ship, never that Chough's records may not be written;
- more than one named gate that drives a native step, naming the gates to record one at a time.

A named gate that drives a native step SHALL run it as the decided human (REQ-records-008) before any gate is closed.

Acceptance Criteria
- `gate list` numbers each open gate with a summary naming what changed, the tests, the risks and a diff link, at most 24 lines, and the SHA-256 digest of its text; the list is saved under `.chough/local/gate-lists/` and no tracked file changes.
- One `gate record` reply naming two listed gates closes both, each relay keeping the same words and its own summary digest; a gate left off the reply stays open.
- An unknown list, a number not listed, a gate no longer open and a summary changed since listing are each refused with nothing written, and listing again then recording succeeds.
- A gate whose change is verifying is refused, naming `chough change ship` with `--list` and `--gate`, which then ships and closes it with its digest.
- Two named gates that both drive a native step are refused with nothing run or written; one such gate with gates that drive nothing runs its step once and closes all of them.
- #190: with a one-line product edit, 300 changed records under `.chough/` and `knowledge/`, and 200 files merged from main after the base, the summary counts one file and names it.
- For a second native change on one branch, the summary's what changed counts only that change's own files since its `base_commit`, not the earlier change's; with default-branch work merged in after it began, it counts from the merge base, as #190's criterion requires.
- At a scope gate, the summary's what changed counts and names the change's deltas and plan under `.specsync/changes/<id>/` first, while its `state.json` and `approvals.json` stay left out.
- With a verifying change's review gate open, `gate list` ends naming `chough change ship <id> --list <list> --gate <n>` for it and offers no `gate record` for it, and the `gate record` refusal gives the ship as its reason, with no claim that Chough's records may not be written.
- At a scope gate whose change has more than five Markdown files, the summary names the delta and the requirement IDs it adds or modifies before the other files.
- At an intent gate with no native change recorded, the summary names the session's criterion IDs and their HI files instead of an unknown base.
- With a change's delta and plan written but not committed, the scope gate's summary counts them and names the delta first, as it does after the commit.
- At an intent gate with no native change, the summary gives each referenced criterion's ID and sentence and no diff line; a delta that only adds says adds, and one that adds and modifies names each.
- A gate's summary names its change as `Change: <id> - <title> (<state>)`, with no em dash (#278).
- A session whose passing evidence came from `chough evidence add --criterion <id>` with no case shows that evidence in the summary's Tests line as passed, not `0 passed`.
- With the change's work not committed yet, the diff line is `git diff <base>` and says the work is not committed; once it is committed, the line is the range to HEAD again.
- A session started before the repository's first commit counts what changed from that first commit and says no base commit was recorded and why.

applied_items.content:
New-project native setup hint. When a native SpecSync configuration exists but `.specsync/sdd.json` is absent or sets `enabled` to false, `chough next` SHALL report the approved-delta line as ``not checked: native SDD is disabled; run `specsync change adopt` to gate stages``, and the `ungated:sdd-disabled` gate detail shown by `next`, `status` and stage moves SHALL name `specsync change adopt`. Without a native configuration the line SHALL remain `not checked: no native lifecycle` and the gate `ungated:not-configured`; an invalid policy SHALL keep `refused:sdd-policy-invalid` and `not checked: SDD policy invalid`. The helper SHALL NOT run `specsync change adopt` or write the policy. While the session's plan or accept stage is ungated this way (`ungated:not-configured` or `ungated:sdd-disabled`) and holds no closed human gate, a stage move SHALL still pass it, but `chough stage advance` SHALL say plainly on that move, and the summary of the move into done SHALL say, that no human decision is recorded for that stage; `chough stage advance --to <stage>` across such a plan or accept SHALL refuse with nothing written, as `refused:no-human-decision`, unless `--reason <text>` is given, naming `--reason`, and the reason, checked for leaks as any recorded text is (REQ-records-006), SHALL land in the Timeline entry of that move (#390, Leif's decision B of 2026-11-19). The walkthrough SHALL begin with a new-project setup path covering a minimal HI criteria file, `specsync init` and scaffolded module files, `specsync change adopt`, and what `ungated:sdd-disabled` means. Trace: LIFE-9, LIFE-6, LIFE-7.

Acceptance Criteria
- With SpecSync configured and `.specsync/sdd.json` absent or `enabled: false`, `chough next` (JSON and text) shows the adopt hint on the approved-delta line, and the `ungated:sdd-disabled` gate detail in `next` and `status` names `specsync change adopt`.
- Without a SpecSync configuration the line stays `not checked: no native lifecycle` with no hint, and an invalid policy still reads `not checked: SDD policy invalid` with no hint.
- The walkthrough begins with the new-project setup path.
- Without a native configuration, `stage advance --to done` from intent refuses as `refused:no-human-decision` naming `--reason`, with nothing written; with `--reason "<text>"` it moves to done, says no human decision is recorded for plan and accept, and the Timeline holds the reason.
- Without a native configuration, a single `stage advance` from plan says no human decision is recorded for plan and moves; with a closed human gate held at plan it says nothing of the kind.

applied_items.content:
Doctor findings and fixes. `chough doctor` (REQ-cli-055) SHALL find this debt without a native read, and its fixes SHALL use Chough's own steps:
- `unmigrated`: a 0.5.x record (REQ-records-010). The fix SHALL name `chough migrate` and SHALL NOT migrate.
- `leak`: a committed record that matches REQ-records-006, with its file, line and kind and never the text. The fix SHALL name `chough doctor --fix --redact`, which SHALL redact the matches in place and is not a decision, except a match in an ID, a front matter line that gives a record's `id`, its aliases or an ID it references (REQ-records-003): `--redact` SHALL never rewrite an ID, since a redacted ID no longer reads. That finding SHALL name the recovery instead, `chough session shelve <id>` for a session record and a reviewed hand edit for any other record, and SHALL stay `skipped` under `--fix --redact`, while the other matches of the same record are redacted.
- `stale_pointer`: the active pointer names a session that is missing or archived. The fix SHALL remove the pointer.
- `finished_session`: an open session that is finished (REQ-history-006) and has no open awaiting-human gate. The fix SHALL archive it. A session with unfolded inbox entries SHALL instead be `skipped`, naming `chough inbox fold`.
- `unfinished_archive`: a session folder whose story exists and that still holds files. The fix SHALL remove every file in the folder whose bytes are committed at HEAD (REQ-records-012), except two kinds it SHALL keep, so no work is lost (#381): an evidence entry, with the screenshot beside it, that the story does not hold, which is one unless one of the story's receipts has the entry's ID and agrees with the receipt the entry gives now in every field it holds (REQ-history-006), so a story an earlier release wrote, with fewer fields, still holds its entries, and an entry that differs from its receipt is kept too; and any file under `agent/inbox/` outside its `folded/` folder. It SHALL remove nothing while the session's story is not committed at HEAD as it is, and the finding SHALL then name it to commit first, so the folder never goes while the story is the session's only record and is not committed (#389). The fix SHALL also name the session's journal post among the files to commit while it is not committed at HEAD, so following it commits the post too; an untracked or ignored journal post still does not hold the finish (#389). A merge that keeps main's archive of a session to which a branch added evidence or an inbox entry leaves such an entry. The finding SHALL then be `skipped`, naming each kept entry, that the story does not hold it, and the way out by hand: keep an evidence entry by moving it with `git mv`, with the screenshot beside it, into an open session's `evidence/` folder and committing that, or drop it with `git rm` in a reviewed commit; for an unfolded inbox entry that `chough inbox add` takes again as it is, add its text again in an open session with `chough inbox add`, then drop the kept copy with `git rm` in a reviewed commit, and for any other kept inbox file, copy what is needed from it, then drop it with `git rm` in a reviewed commit; then run `chough doctor --fix` again. macOS metadata in the folder (REQ-cli-068), committed or not, SHALL be removed with it and never block the fix (#377). Any other file it keeps SHALL be reported as `skipped`, naming the commit to make.
- `stale_gates`: an open session whose native change is archived on HEAD and that has open awaiting-human gates. This fix is a decision. With `--reason`, it SHALL withdraw those gates as `chough checkpoint --clear-awaiting-human` does, recording no human decision, SHALL write that reason, in the person's words and checked as REQ-records-006 checks any written value, as the `withdrawn` field of each withdrawn gate's `gate-closed` entry, so the archived story says why each gate was withdrawn, and SHALL then archive the session as the `finished_session` fix does. A decision fix that was applied SHALL echo the reason it wrote in its finding as `decision_reason`.
- `unfinished_session`: an open, unfinished session named with `--close <id>`. This fix is a decision. With `--reason`, it SHALL close the session as `chough session close <id> --reason` does.
- `timeline_rewritten`: a session or story whose Timeline at HEAD is not an exact prefix of its working Timeline (REQ-history-002). It has no fix; the finding names the entries that differ. An entry SHALL NOT count as rewritten when it equals what redaction makes of HEAD's entry, checked by redacting HEAD's text again as `chough doctor --fix --redact` does, since restoring it would restore the leak; committing the redaction is the way on (#374). Any other difference, a hand edit that writes `<redacted:<kind>>` over ordinary words included, still counts.
- `stale_bug_links`: a bug whose body links an open session's evidence entry that left with its archived session, while that session's story holds it as a receipt. The finding names each such entry and the story. The fix, which is not a decision, SHALL append one Log entry to the bug that links each entry to the archived story (REQ-cli-012) and SHALL change no earlier line; a bug whose body already links the story for an entry is not found for it.
- `alias_conflict`: an ID that is the `id` or alias of two records (REQ-records-003). It has no fix; the finding names both records.
- `oversize`: a committed record, evidence entry or screenshot over its bound (REQ-records-001, REQ-records-005, REQ-records-013). It has no fix; the finding names the file, its size and the bound, and the verify lane's `leaks` step fails on it as it does on `leak`, so CI refuses an oversized receipt.
- `unreadable`: a committed Chough record under `.chough/` that its reader refuses, such as front matter outside the subset of REQ-records-001, which makes `chough status` and `chough next` refuse the project.
